objectives: Recognize 47,XXY karyotype as the most common sex chromosome aneuploidy in males
Identify classic clinical pentad: tall stature, gynecomastia, small firm testes, infertility, learning/behavioral issues
Order and interpret the diagnostic workup: karyotype, FSH/LH (high), total testosterone (low), estradiol
Manage with testosterone replacement timed to puberty, fertility counseling (TESE+ICSI), and surveillance for comorbidities
Differentiate from Kallmann syndrome, androgen insensitivity, primary testicular failure of other etiologies
high_yield_facts: Most common sex chromosome aneuploidy in males (~1:600 live male births)
Diagnosis confirmed by karyotype, NOT by hormone levels alone
Increased risk: breast cancer (20-50x baseline male), mediastinal germ cell tumors, osteoporosis, T2DM, venous thromboembolism
Most cases due to maternal meiotic nondisjunction; advanced maternal age is a risk factor
